author: Sushiguyy
quote:
What has happened to Rockstar? 

First off there’s no disc so you can’t return the game or resell it if you don’t like it. The game is also locked in at 30 FPS and it frequently drops lower than that during intense moments. How is that acceptable for a game with this much money behind it?

The characters are super annoying and bland, Jason has the personality of a plank of wood, and the story is so bad and poorly written. The physics feel off compared to the older GTAs, and the movement is way too heavy and sluggish. It feels more like Red Dead Redemption II than GTA, and not in a good way.

And why is so much of the gameplay so boring? For example at the start of the game it makes you do household chores and run errands. I bought GTA, not The Sims. The relationship between Lucia and Jason is also painfully cringe.

The humour is another massive letdown. GTA used to parody and make fun of absolutely everything, and that’s what made it so good. Now the jokes barely land or are just not funny, the satire is heavily watered down, and the game takes itself far too seriously. Prostitutes have been removed from the game, you can’t attack certain groups of people such as protesters, and you can’t even steal the cars around your neighbourhood. I thought this was supposed to be Grand Theft Auto! 

With so many of the old writers gone, it really shows. The older games had memorable characters, brilliant humour, and their own personality. Rockstar has completely lost sight of what GTA is supposed to be.

I’ll give it credit for the graphics and some of the open-world gameplay, but that’s about it. GTA 6 is an absolute disgrace to the franchise, and this is coming from someone who loves all the previous GTAs.

author: Sushiguyy
quote:
Mario Kart World forgot what makes Mario Kart fun.

I really tried to like this game. When I first started Mario Kart World, I thought it looked great. The presentation is polished, the characters have loads of personality, the world is impressive, and some of the proper circuits are genuinely really good. But the more I played, the more frustrated I became. My biggest problem is the track design. There are far too many long, wide, straight roads. Mario Kart is at its best when you’re constantly drifting around corners, learning the course, improving your racing line and looking for shortcuts. In Mario Kart World, I often feel like I’m just holding accelerate and driving forwards. The Grand Prix structure makes this even worse. You can start a cup with a proper Mario Kart circuit and have a great time, then the next race sends you down a long connecting road for most of the race. Eventually you reach the actual circuit, and then you only get one lap of it. That is probably the part I dislike most. I want to race the tracks. I don’t want to spend most of the race travelling to them. The sense of speed also feels much weaker than it did in Mario Kart 8 Deluxe. Even 150cc often feels strangely slow. There are certain boosted sections, like parts of Bowser’s Castle, where the game suddenly feels fast and exciting, and that actually reminded me of how 150cc felt normally in Mario Kart 8 Deluxe. Then you leave the boost section and the game immediately feels slow again. I also don’t understand why 200cc still isn’t available. With roads this wide and open, this feels like the perfect Mario Kart game for 200cc. The 24-player races sound great on paper, but in practice they become complete item chaos. You can be driving well and then get hit several times in a row and disappear into a massive pack of racers. Another thing that really disappointed me was the removal of country flags from online multiplayer. In Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, I loved joining a lobby and seeing where everyone was from. Seeing players from Japan, the UK, America, France, Germany, Australia and other countries made online racing feel genuinely international. It created a fun sense of friendly competition between different countries and gave the lobbies more personality. Now we have a game called Mario Kart World, and somehow the country flags are gone. I genuinely do not understand that decision. It might sound like a small thing, but it added a lot to the online experience. There are definitely things I like about Mario Kart World. It looks great, some of the circuits are excellent, and I can see what Nintendo was trying to do with the open-world idea. But I think the game has lost too much of what made Mario Kart 8 Deluxe so much fun. I would much rather have four proper circuits in a Grand Prix, three laps on each one, more corners, more drifting, a stronger sense of speed, 200cc, and the country flags back online. Bigger does not automatically mean better. 

For now, I’m returning Mario Kart World and going back to Mario Kart 8 Deluxe. 

Don’t waste your money on this mediocre game.
